text:
sam_perkins: heads-up — canary (us-east, go-client v0.12.2) is showing streaming requests that never finish when the caller cancels the context quickly (<100ms after first token). goroutine leaks observed.

maya_chen: repro steps?

sam_perkins: minimal: create req with req = http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", "/v1/chat/stream", body), client.Do(req) and cancel ctx after first chunk arrives. sometimes the stream never returns, conn stays ESTABLISHED. logs show an http2 stream error CANCEL then silence.

evan_ng: can you paste the log snippet?

sam_perkins: sure — trimmed: 

```
2026-03-14T16:12:05.123Z INFO stream=chat id=7 recv chunk
2026-03-14T16:12:05.130Z INFO stream=chat id=7 ctx cancelled
2026-03-14T16:12:05.131Z WARN http2: stream error: stream ID 7; CANCEL
# then nothing — goroutine stuck in net/http.(*http2clientStream).readBody
```

zara_khan: interesting. are we seeing connections pile up on the client side?

sam_perkins: yes — netstat shows many ESTABLISHED to server, goroutine dump shows stalled http2 reader goroutines. we tried with default http.Transport config + ForceAttemptHTTP2 = true, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=200, IdleConnTimeout=90s.

infra-bot: infra noticed increased file descriptors for the canary host around the same time.

maya_chen: could be cancellation not being translated into a transport-level RST_STREAM. server might keep streaming and client stuck waiting. which Go runtime are we using on canary?

sam_perkins: go1.20.8. I've seen similar reports in older issues about context cancel not closing http2 conn unless resp.Body.Close is called. but when the request hangs we never get a resp to close.

evan_ng: two quick guesses: 1) server doesn't honor client reset, 2) client http2 stack has a race where stream is marked error but reader goroutine still blocks on a frame read. we should capture h2 frames (nghttp2 or tshark) to confirm.

maya_chen: i pushed a local test harness to quickly cancel streams in a tight loop. reproduces reliably on my laptop with a patched server.

sam_perkins: for a short-term mitigation i experimented with a cancel-aware RoundTripper wrapper that calls CloseIdleConnections for that transport when the request ctx cancels (hacky but seems to free stuck goroutines). snippet: 

```go
// cancelRT : cheap workaround that nukes idle conns on ctx cancel
type cancelRT struct{ rt http.RoundTripper }
func (c *cancelRT) RoundTrip(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
  ctx := req.Context()
  // best-effort: only call CloseIdleConnections if underlying is *http.Transport
  if t, ok := c.rt.(*http.Transport); ok {
    go func() {
      <-ctx.Done()
      t.CloseIdleConnections()
    }()
  }
  return c.rt.RoundTrip(req)
}
```

zara_khan: that will tear down reuse for that host for a moment, but it's opt-in and cheap for canary. might be acceptable while we debug.

evan_ng: long-term we should: 1) capture full h2 frame trace 2) add integration test that cancels after first token 3) try go1.21 on canary (http2 fixes landed) 4) consider making client explicitly send RST_STREAM when ctx canceled if transport supports it.

maya_chen: note — calling req.Close = true before Do will force connection close after request, which avoids reuse but prevents this hang. downside: higher connection churn.

sam_perkins: agreed. plan I'm proposing:
- open PR adding Cancel-aware wrapper behind env toggle RW_H2_CANCEL_WORKAROUND=true
- add canary job that runs the cancel stress test for 24h with and without workaround
- collect tcpdump + nghttp2 frames for at least one repro
- try upgrade canary to go1.21 in parallel

zara_khan: i can run the 24h job and collect metrics (goroutine count, FD count, idle conns). will add an alert if goroutine delta > 200.

evan_ng: if you do the wrapper PR, add unit test for the wrapper behavior and a clear comment linking to the issue and why it's opt-in.

sam_perkins: will do. i'll also attach my small repro harness and the raw logs to the PR. thanks — ping me if you want to run the repro locally (includes a dockerized server). :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deployed canary with RW_H2_CANCEL_WORKAROUND=true to canary-us-east; collection enabled.

sam_perkins: awesome — i'll follow up with the PR later today.
